summary.en: Haitian security forces have retaken the national stadium after two years of gang control, while Salvadoran missiles and ground forces struck a gang hideout, destroying the Mawozo headquarters and killing about 20 gang members. The UN chief condemned an attack that killed 47 people and the United Nations reported more than 1,000 deaths between July and September. Haitian police killed a gang leader and intensified operations against other sites, and kidnappings in the capital rose in the third quarter. 193 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Haitis sikkerhetsstyrker har tatt tilbake nasjonalstadion etter to år med gjengkontroll, mens salvadoranske missiler og bakkestyrker rammet et gjengskjul, ødela Mawozo-hovedkvarteret og drepte omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer. FN-sjefen fordømte et angrep som drepte 47 personer, og De forente nasjoner rapporterte mer enn 1 000 dødsfall mellom juli og september. Haitisk politi drepte en gjengleder og intensiverte operasjoner mot andre steder, og kidnappinger i hovedstaden steg i tredje kvartal. 193 kamprelaterte dødsfall skjedde i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
